market_question: Will the US acquire part of Greenland in 2026?
reasoning: The US acquiring part of Greenland is extremely unlikely given strong opposition from Denmark and Greenland, domestic treaty hurdles, and no plausible use of force. Even if a pro-acquisition president took office in 2025, achieving a binding agreement by end of 2026 is a remote prospect, well below the market's 14.5% implied probability.
evidence_points: Denmark and Greenland have consistently and publicly refused any sale or transfer of territory.
Any formal acquisition would likely require a treaty ratified by a 2/3 US Senate vote, an immense political challenge.
No substantive negotiations or legal frameworks toward acquisition exist, and the time horizon is very short.
sources_consulted: Historical context of Trump's Greenland proposal
